html:
SMTO-EXE-0007 — SMTO couldn't start the command

GUID: 045a2b71-eefa-4c6e-afb6-c0757c779529
Slug: process-failed-to-start
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The command never began running, so it made no changes. Usually the computer that runs commands isn't connected or set up, or that computer refused to start the program.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the message box, open the Execution target menu, select Refresh targets, and pick a Gateway that shows a check mark. The command needs a connected Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, and none was ready.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. If it isn't connected, make sure its computer is on and the Gateway program is running. A Gateway that is offline, not set up, or out of date can't start any command.
  3. Read the message under the command in the task. If it names a missing program or a permission problem, install that program or fix the permission on that computer. Sometimes the Gateway is fine but the computer itself refuses to start the program.
  4. Once the cause is fixed, ask SMTO to run the task again. Nothing ran the first time, so running it again won't repeat any changes.

What success looks like

  • The command shows output in the task instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up SMTO or the Gateway. Don't keep resending the same request unchanged; it will fail the same way until the cause is fixed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The command was not executed (process_state=failed_to_start) because a launch prerequisite failed: missing or disconnected Gateway configuration, Gateway job admission or authorization change, temp-path mapping failure, or an OS process-spawn error.

What this means

  • Execution reported failed-to-start or a known unexecuted launch failure. Producers include missing Gateway configuration, job admission/launch failure and OS spawn failure; the category does not identify one OS cause. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Execution reported failed-to-start or a known unexecuted launch failure. Producers include missing Gateway configuration, job admission/launch failure and OS spawn failure; the category does not identify one OS cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained launch or configuration reason, execution flag and process state before checking executable, path or permissions.

How to fix it

  • Read the receipt's error/stderr to identify the producer: GatewayConfigurationError (default node not configured, outbound Gateway not connected, endpoint/TLS record conflict, resource-locking policy upgrade required), Gateway admission (gateway_authorization_changed, purge/update guard), tmp_mapping_failed, or OSError from subprocess.Popen. Fix that prerequisite (Gateway record and connection, Gateway version, shell path, permissions), then start a new operation; executed=false means no effect occurred.
  • Correct the specific configuration, admission or OS launch failure shown in the receipt, then verify any new launch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific failed prerequisite is corrected and a new authorized operation obtains a valid launch receipt.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
